text:
ShiroFOC closes motor-control loops locally and communicates with a coordinating motherboard over CAN. This presentation follows the current connected KiCad redraw. It explains the released circuit, documented calculations and engineering tradeoffs. The schematic is ready for first-prototype PCB layout. It is not a fabrication release or a hardware qualification. Current and thermal values remain design targets.

They are not demonstrated ratings. An 80 A instantaneous peak cannot be commissioned while a +60 A comparator trip is active. text:
Field-oriented control transforms measured phase currents into a rotor-related coordinate system. Current regulators control torque-producing and field-related components, then modulation generates complementary PWM. The position sensor provides the rotor-angle reference. Integration reduces component count and pin-level interconnects, while external MOSFETs allow package and loss selection. This is an explanation of the intended control architecture, not a claim that firmware already implements it. Sources: DESIGN_CONSTRAINTS.md, Fixed architecture, and FIRMWARE_BRINGUP_CONTRACT.md.

The parallel electrolytics provide 2.04 mF nominal capacitance. At 42 V the stored energy is 0.5 × 0.00204 × 42² = 1.799 J. text:
The 10 nF capacitor returns above the current shunt and the 1 µF capacitor returns to ground, so layout must preserve the intended local loop. Gate resistors belong at MOSFET gate pins. The NTC must couple thermally without introducing a signal path on the switch-node island. The inductor manufacturer specifies a central copper keepout. The DYD LDO thermal pad is ground, whereas the phase power block thermal VIN pad is at bus potential. Brake leads must remain short and appropriately rated. Footprint compatibility cannot be inferred from package outline alone. The current release supplies resolved footprints, but PCB placement, routing, DRC and thermal qualification remain future work. Sources: PCB_LAYOUT_HANDOFF.md and PCB_LAYOUT_GUIDELINES.md.

The firmware contract requires explicit arming with fresh commands, no automatic stale-command restart, feedback mux enable followed by at least 2 ms settling, ADC/op-amp calibration and comparator/DAC setup before PWM. Then configure STSPIN interlocking, protection and 10 V VCC, check READY/NFAULT and verify temperature and bus plausibility. Test battery-only, USB-only and both connection orders with current limiting and external precharge. Install the qualified brake resistor before regenerative operation. Use appropriate differential/isolated probing for switching nodes rather than connecting an earth-referenced probe ground to a phase. This is a commissioning sequence, not a record of completed measurements. Source: FIRMWARE_BRINGUP_CONTRACT.md, Hardware commissioning sequence.

The main choices are an STSPIN32G4 with external 3.3 V logic power, 10 V gate drive, three 60 V power blocks, three low-side shunts, a local 100 V brake switch and configurable position feedback. The project reports zero schematic ERC violations and net/footprint consistency checks, which support proceeding to layout. These checks cannot prove switching safety, continuous current, thermal behavior or energy handling. The strongest open items are the DC-link ripple rating, snubber population around maximum bus voltage, bootstrap refresh margin and the reconciliation of the 80 A target with initial +60 A protection. Sources: SCHEMATIC_REDRAW_REVIEW.md and DESIGN_REVIEW_REV_A.md.

The worksheet distinguishes sourced part values from model inputs and measured quantities. Qg = 56 nC maximum is for 10 V drive at the TI stated 30 V/30 A conditions; Qgd = 7 nC is typical. Ceff cannot be finalized without a capacitor MPN and bias curve. At 20 kHz the period is 50 µs. Pull-down charge at 10 V is 5 nC over that full period. Adding that to Qg gives at least 61 nC before driver quiescent/leakage charge, corresponding to 0.61 V at nominal 100 nF. The startup RC estimate is illustrative. A VCC reservoir sharing charge with three initially empty 100 nF capacitors has ideal instantaneous sag 10×0.3/(10+0.3) ≈ 0.291 V when expressed in µF, before other effects. VM filter settling ignores the small mux on-resistance and ADC acquisition disturbances. Shunt loss at 80 A is instantaneous. For the comparator network use RU = 450 kΩ, RL = 12.7 kΩ and RF = 1 MΩ. The comparator reference is nominally 1.242 V, with input offset and internal hysteresis included as appropriate. The project calculation records 45.919 V rising and 44.213 V falling and applies component corner allowances; it is not a dynamic switching simulation. Without both logic and gate supplies the brake cannot act. No fitted sensing proves resistor continuity. For the mechanical example, omega is 209.44 rad/s and energy is 219.32 J. At a repeated stop frequency r, average rotational energy dumping alone is approximately 219.32r watts, before gravity or externally supplied work. Source: electrical_calculations.json brake section and DESIGN_REVIEW_REV_A.md.
